directions.opportunity: validateRecordStructure builds all four model-object maps separately for each of its three available() calls, then discards three maps from every build.
directions.impact: For every structure validation with a present model, construct four maps once instead of twelve. Eliminate two complete traversals and two sets of object copies for every model collection, including the relationship collection whose map is not used by reference validation.
evidence: src/core/record/structure.ts:182-188: modelObjects eagerly maps and copies elements, relationships, Element Kinds and Relationship Kinds into four new Maps.
src/core/record/structure.ts:216-223: available calls modelObjects(model)[type], retains only one map, then overlays that structure type.
src/core/record/structure.ts:227-231: validateRecordStructure calls available three times for the same model, for elements, elementKinds and relationshipKinds.

src/core/record/workspace.ts:234,269 and src/commands/record.ts:176: create, update and validate use this deterministic validation boundary. The target implementation file is tracked and appears in git diff 17fd82bca9a2a8aa4c0f2f69297390965e7cacb0...HEAD --name-only.
directions.recommendation: Build modelObjects once within validateRecordStructure and pass the independent map for each requested type into the private overlay helper. Keep maps local to the invocation.
directions.keyDesign: Create one invocation-local set of the existing four model maps when model is non-null. available receives the selected fresh map and overlays only structure[type]. When model is null, supply separate empty maps. Keep compareStructure and exported function signatures unchanged.
preservationConstraints: Retain structure overlay order, field merging, removed:true deletion, and the distinction between absent fields and parent:null. Each type must receive its own Map.
Retain current Map construction semantics for repeated keys: the last model object wins; apply record overlays in their existing sequence. Do not add deduplication or validation.
Preserve root normalization to root === true and shallow object-copy semantics, including isolation from the input model and input structure.
Keep diagnostic severity, code, identity, field, message and ordering identical: Element checks first, Relationship checks next, then Kind reference checks, preserving source-array and field order.

Preserve null-model initial Build behavior, public APIs, thrown RecordStructureError behavior and caller error timing. Do not cache across calls or reuse maps between create/update/validate or consume revalidation boundaries.

Preserve schemaVersion 4, nature/decision semantics, sourceVersion checks, filesystem operations and all Element Contracts. This direction changes only in-memory preparation inside structure validation.
implementationOutline: Move the present-model modelObjects invocation to the beginning of validateRecordStructure, before constructing the three available maps.
Change only the private available helper to overlay its supplied type-specific map; pass distinct maps or distinct empty maps for a null model.
Keep all validation loops and diagnostic emission unchanged; verify that input model objects and record objects remain unmodified across repeated calls.
validation: Baseline executed: pnpm exec vitest run test/core/record/structure.test.ts test/core/record/coverage.test.ts test/core/record/consume.test.ts test/core/record/workspace.test.ts — 4 files / 52 tests passed. Rerun after implementation.
Existing structure tests assert ordered diagnostics for unknown Kinds, deleted parents, unresolved Relationship endpoints and invalid Project Root, and verify a Build record without a formal model.

Extend the existing structure behavior test with successive validations that add/remove/override the same model identities; assert expected ordered diagnostics and exact before/after equality of the model and record structures, proving no overlay leakage or input mutation.

Statically verify one modelObjects invocation per present-model validateRecordStructure call, with no invocation remaining inside the overlay helper; this proves the eliminated work without a workload-dependent latency claim.
directions.priorityReason: Ranks first because every present-model structure validation currently repeats complete model indexing and object copying three times. Removing two whole builds has a broader unconditional effect than eliminating one duplicate location-text resolution per covered Element detail.

directions.opportunity: A resolved Element coverage detail calls locationText once to establish location existence and again to retrieve the exact same text for quote matching.
directions.impact: Resolve each valid Element detail once instead of twice, removing one element/Section/Acceptance Case search and one text construction per resolved Element detail. For a Section location this also removes a duplicate flatMap allocation and join over its Acceptance Cases.
evidence: src/core/record/coverage.ts:128-137: locationText searches model elements, then Sections and Acceptance Cases, and constructs Declaration, Section or Acceptance Case text.
src/core/record/coverage.ts:145-146: resolves delegates every Element location to locationText solely to compare its result with undefined.

src/core/record/coverage.ts:218-221: after resolves succeeds, checkCoverage immediately calls locationText again for quote matching against the same model and location. No mutation or await separates these calls.
src/core/record/coverage.ts:259-266: recordCoverage uses checkCoverage before any coverage write. This implementation file is tracked and belongs to the immutable base scope.
directions.recommendation: Within the existing detail-validation branch, retain the Element location text returned by the first resolution and reuse it for existence and quote checks.
directions.keyDesign: After the current detail-key, uncovered, location-shape and quote-presence checks succeed, use a local branch for Element locations: compute locationText once, treat only undefined as unresolved, otherwise apply the existing comparableText/includes check to that value. Preserve resolves for non-Element locations or narrow that private helper to the remaining variants. Avoid a new global index or cache.
preservationConstraints: Keep input-shape and empty-quote validation before model resolution, and preserve the exact diagnostic precedence and messages for malformed input, uncovered details, unresolved locations and missing quotes.
Preserve first-match Array.find semantics for elements, Sections and Acceptance Cases, including repeated keys in any model admitted by the existing callers. Do not replace find with a last-wins Map.

Distinguish undefined from an existing empty Section body: an empty string is a resolved location. Preserve exact title/definition, Section plus Acceptance Case, and Acceptance Case name/body concatenation.
Retain comparableText exactly: remove asterisks, underscores and backticks and all whitespace before substring matching. Do not add case folding, Unicode normalization or semantic interpretation.
Preserve submitted entry/detail order and duplicates, all pending/accepted/excluded/informative dispositions, missing-result detection and complete ordered diagnostics.

Keep non-Element identity resolution, saved coverage bytes and schema, sourceVersion and target fingerprint binding, write timing, failure no-write behavior, managed paths and fresh consume gates unchanged.
implementationOutline: Retain the existing validation guards before resolving a detail location.
Resolve and retain one text value for an Element location; issue the existing unresolved diagnostic only when it is undefined, then check the quote using that same text.
Keep non-Element resolution and all persistence paths unchanged; remove the now-unneeded duplicate Element resolution path.
validation: Rerun test/core/record/coverage.test.ts and test/core/record/consume.test.ts after implementation; the freshly executed baseline included all 33 tests in these two files and passed.

Existing coverage cases verify whitespace-insensitive matching, Section and Acceptance Case locations, wrong-location quotes, nonexistent cases, malformed quote shape, dispositions, stale source versions and failure without creating coverage output.

Extend the existing coverage rejection cases to compare complete ordered diagnostics for multiple invalid details, and exercise Declaration text and emphasis normalization, confirming unchanged observable resolution behavior.

Review the final detail control flow to prove each resolved Element detail invokes locationText only once, without moving any filesystem reads, writes or consume revalidation. No benchmark or cache-hit assumption is required.
directions.priorityReason: Ranks second: the redundant resolution is unconditional for resolved Element details and its removal is small and behavior-local, but the avoided work is narrower than repeated full-model indexing in structure validation. It is independent of the first direction.
